title: StratusWare Private VPC Discovery
summary: Discovery for StratusWare evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) deployment. Main topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region constraints (eu-west-1 required), KMS/CMK, audit logs, SSO/SAML, network egress and NAT, dedicated capacity sizing. Agreed next steps: send security docs, network diagram, schedule technical deep dive and pilot benchmark.
next_steps: Maya to send SOC2 + security whitepaper and network diagram (by 2026-03-06)
Schedule SE-led technical deep dive for VPC peering and private endpoints (by 2026-03-10)
Customer to share CIDR ranges and target region constraints (eu-west-1)
action_items: Maya Chen - send SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and reference network diagram - due 2026-03-06
Luis Ortega - prepare proposed architecture for PrivateLink vs VPC Peering including port/IP mapping - due 2026-03-09
Mark Bennett - provide VPC CIDRs, Transit Gateway design, and expected egress pattern - due 2026-03-08
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I can see Anjali, Mark, Samir, great. we scheduled 45 minutes, we actually have about 49, so uh we'll try and keep it tight. quick intros?
[00:15] Anjali Rao: yeah hi I'm Anjali, CTO at StratusWare, we run a multi-tenant analytics platform, we're exploring hosted vs private for inference, mainly around data residency and latency.
[00:28] Mark Bennett: Mark, head infra. we manage our AWS and GCP footprint but primary workloads are in eu-west-1.
[00:33] Samir Patel: Samir, security eng. I'm focused on encryption, audit logs, and the network boundary.
[00:39] Maya Chen: Perfect. On our side I'm Maya, AE, and Luis is our SE to go deep on networking.
[00:45] Luis Ortega: hey all, thanks, i'll jump into the architecture questions; quick note, apologies for any auto-transcribe weirdness, sometimes PrivateLink turns into private link, oh wait it is private link, okay.
[00:55] Anjali Rao: ha, yeah so our starting point: regulatory requirement says eu-west-1 for inference, can't cross region. latency needs to be < 120ms p95 for our web UI flow. cost target is, we don't want to go crazy on reserved GPUs until we validate throughput.
[01:12] Maya Chen: Understood. Two immediate options: hosted (our hosted API) with region pinned to eu-west-1 where available, or Redwood Private-style deployment in your VPC. Private gives you private endpoints, no public egress, CMK integration for keys, and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM.
[01:29] Mark Bennett: Can you talk network specifics — VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit Gateway? our infra uses TGW and we prefer not to open peering for every vendor.
[01:40] Luis Ortega: Absolutely. Short answer: we support both VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints). With TGW the pattern we recommend is: deploy Redwood Private into a customer-controlled account or a managed account with ENIs in subnets; then connect via PrivateLink to avoid route table changes across spokes. Peering is simpler but can get messy at scale.
[02:01] Samir Patel: For compliance we need to ensure no internet egress and full control over VPC flow logs, KMS CMK for model keys, and audit logs accessible. Does Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
[02:12] Luis Ortega: Yes, we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for at-rest encryption and can integrate with your KMS for key rotation. Audit logs — we can stream to your CloudWatch or S3 via a cross-account role, or forward to your SIEM. Note: some of the forwarding requires setting up an IAM role we assume.
[02:30] Anjali Rao: About endpoints — if we use PrivateLink what's the bandwidth/latency expectation? we're serving hundreds of requests per second but with short contexts, many small inference calls.
[02:42] Luis Ortega: PrivateLink adds minimal latency, typically single-digit ms in-region. The main constraint is concurrent connections per ENI. We suggested patterns: use a pool of ENIs across AZs, and enable HTTP/2 or gRPC multiplexing to keep connections low. Also consider batching on the client side to reduce per-token cost.
[03:05] Mark Bennett: Connection limits are our concern, we already use API gateways with NLBs. how many ENIs do you require?
[03:12] Luis Ortega: It depends on throughput and concurrent requests; rough thumb: for 100 rps with low tokens per call, a modest pool of 6-10 ENIs across AZs should be fine. we'll propose sizing in the follow-up architecture doc.
[03:25] Anjali Rao: Ok. SSO and SAML — we need strict RBAC and SAML 2.0 integration with our IdP; do you support SCIM for user provisioning?
[03:35] Maya Chen: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning and RBAC at the org and project level. For Private deployments we can integrate with your AD/IdP via SAML.
[03:44] Samir Patel: Data retention and logs: we want to ensure no PII leaves VPC. Are prompt logs stored outside customer's control?
[03:52] Luis Ortega: Default behavior for Private is that logs and inputs stay in your environment — we can disable telemetry forwarding. For hosted API we'd retain traces for debugging but can turn off storage or set strict retention. We'll include the exact fields collected in the security deck.
[04:08] Anjali Rao: Good. region constraint again — do you have infra options in eu-west-1 for Private?
[04:15] Maya Chen: yes, we currently run Private deployments in eu-west-1 and some other EMEA regions; if there's a specific AZ requirement we can accommodate but we need to plan capacity.
[04:25] Mark Bennett: Pricing: we might start with a pilot and then move to dedicated reserved capacity. what's the minimum commit?
[04:33] Maya Chen: For Redwood Dedicated it's typically monthly reserved capacity; pilots can be done via a short-term Dedicated or a private trial in your account. We'll send the pilot pricing options — flexible pilot rates are common.
[04:43] Anjali Rao: For the pilot we want to run our workload against your infra to validate latency and cost. We'll need a benchmark plan.
[04:51] Luis Ortega: We usually run a two-phase benchmark: synthetic load to tune ENIs/batching, then replay real traffic (anonymized) to validate p95 latency and token cost. We'll need your sample traffic and CIDR ranges.
[05:06] Samir Patel: On network security, do you require opening outbound internet to register nodes? we have strict egress rules; any bootstrap calls?
[05:14] Luis Ortega: There are a couple of control-plane endpoints for registration and health that can be done via PrivateLink; otherwise node images can be pre-baked. If your environment is air-gapped we'll discuss an on-prem package. For most customers, no direct public egress is required once PrivateLink is configured.
[05:33] Mark Bennett: OK, that's promising. Does Redwood integrate with AWS Transit Gateway NAT or do you recommend NAT gateways in the management VPC?
[05:42] Luis Ortega: For outbound egress we recommend using NAT in a management VPC or TGW centralized egress. But again with PrivateLink most control-plane traffic can be kept internal. We'll capture these options in the architecture doc.
[05:55] Anjali Rao: Any compliance docs you can share? SOC 2, penetration testing?
[05:59] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share SOC 2 Type II, pen test summary, and our security whitepaper. We'll also include our data flow diagrams.
[06:10] Mark Bennett: On the networking diagram, please highlight route tables and security groups, we need to know port mappings — inference traffic is HTTPS but are there other ports?
[06:20] Luis Ortega: Mostly HTTPS over 443. For debug and metrics we may use a few internal ports but those can be locked down. We'll provide a port/IP breakdown.
[06:32] Anjali Rao: How do you handle fallback if capacity in eu-west-1 is exhausted? we can't fail over to another region for compliance reasons.
[06:41] Maya Chen: We have routing policies: for private deployments you control the capacity; for hosted API we can route to a reserved Dedicated pool or queue requests. But if you require strict in-region only, we recommend Dedicated/Private with capacity planning and burst policies.
[06:57] Mark Bennett: SLA? we need 99.95% for the API surface.
[07:03] Maya Chen: Our Dedicated customers can get SLA-backed throughput and uptime. For Private deployments running in your VPC the uptime depends on the resources you provision but we have recommendations and can offer support SLAs.
[07:16] Samir Patel: Kerberos? We use mTLS internally; can you do mTLS between services?
[07:22] Luis Ortega: We support mutual TLS for service-to-service connections in Private instances, yes. For API clients we support TLS and token-based auth; mTLS is possible with some config.
[07:35] Anjali Rao: On model artifacts and caching — where is the KV cache stored? within the nodes or in a managed cache?
[07:42] Luis Ortega: KV cache lives on the inference nodes for low latency; it's ephemeral and can be persisted to a customer-managed cache (e.g., Redis in your VPC) if you want warm starts across restarts. We'll discuss cache persistence in the doc.
[07:58] Mark Bennett: For the pilot, what telemetry do you need? metrics, traces, logs?
[08:03] Luis Ortega: Metrics (latency, tokens, throughput), basic traces for request flow, and error logs. If you have a preferred APM we can forward traces.
[08:12] Anjali Rao: Great. Any blockers you see?
[08:16] Maya Chen: None immediate. We just need CIDR ranges, desired region (eu-west-1), and sample traffic for benchmarking. We'll follow with the security pack and an architecture doc.
[08:26] Samir Patel: Can you email the architecture doc with red lines for ports we must open? we have a change window next week.
[08:31] Maya Chen: Yep, we'll add the change window note.
[08:33] Mark Bennett: timeline: if we like pilot results we could onboard to dedicated in 8-12 weeks.
[08:39] Maya Chen: Sounds reasonable. we'll propose a pilot plan and timeline.
[08:43] Luis Ortega: One thing to flag: certificate provisioning for PrivateLink endpoint validation sometimes takes 24-48 hours if we need custom certs; we can note that in the timeline.
[08:55] Anjali Rao: ok noted.
[08:58] Maya Chen: Wrap up — recap quick: we'll send SOC2 and security docs, provide architecture options (PrivateLink vs peering + TGW patterns), sizing estimate for ENIs and capacity, and a benchmark plan. Next call SE deep dive scheduled after customer shares CIDRs and sample traffic.
[09:16] Anjali Rao: Thank you.
[09:18] Mark Bennett: thanks all.
[09:20] Samir Patel: thanks.
[09:22] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up.
[09:26] (call ends)

Note: transcription includes occasional misheard words (e.g., "PrivateLink" transcribed as "private link"), and speaker labels simplified; we've kept natural speech patterns, filler words, and interruptions.
